purpose: Independent practice of C1.1 — identifying patterns as repeating, growing, or shrinking AND describing the change from one term to the next, with a real-life context check.
student_learning_goal: I can identify a pattern as repeating, growing, or shrinking and describe what changes from one term to the next.

parts.answer_key: Calendar = GROWING (+1 each day). Bricks = REPEATING (the offset pattern repeats row by row). Hopscotch = GROWING (+1 each square). Cookie = SHRINKING (the cookie gets smaller each frame). Accept synonyms (e.g., 'getting bigger' = growing).

early_finisher_prompt: If you finish, flip the page over and draw THREE more real-life patterns you can think of — one of each type. Label each.
teacher_notes: Lesson 1 consolidation. Distribute at the end of the Action phase. Watch for: (a) on Part 1, children who match all to one type — they may need a re-loop on the three-type distinction. (b) On Part 2, accept '+2', 'two', or 'two more' as the rule. (c) On Part 3, the brick wall is the only repeating example — children who write 'growing' for it likely missed the alternating offset. Use Part 1 + Part 3 as primary diagnostic-tracker evidence.
